LESSON: CARE FOR SCHOOL ENVIRONMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our School
Topic 5.3: Care for School Environment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Care for School Environment, part of Our School in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need a clean environment? 2. How do we clean the school environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Care for School Environment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learner explores solutions to problems by improvising cleaning materials.

Values:
Responsibility: learner fosters self-drive in cleaning working areas after every activity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Personal hygiene: learner picks litter and cleans up a working place to maintain a clean environment.

Link to other learning areas:

Care for the environment relates to cleaning routine in Mathematics Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Adapted litter collection bins which are lighter with handles, lighter and shorter rakes with padded handle rod, brooms, scissors

with enhanced grip, 20-litre Jerry-cans, cartons, old buckets, sisal twines, rubbish pit/ incinerator, Video clips, charts, name

cards, pictures and picture cut outs about cleaning and disposal of waste, theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board,

adapted digital devices, songs and poems about cleaning and disposal of waste, universal cuffs with padded pencils, crayons

with grips, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using lower extremities, book holders and page turners, positioning/ seating

devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/ crutches, head/ mouth

pointers, splints for hands/ hand stabilizers,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe

Core Competencies to be developed:

Digital literacy: learner manipulates digital devices to watch video clips showing dangerous places, objects and activities.

Values:

• Responsibility: learner develops diligence when telling what to do when they meet strangers.

• Integrity: learner develops discipline when cleaning working areas after an activity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

• Safety and security: learner enhances safety and security when able to identify strangers and knowing what to do when in

contact with a stranger.

• Disaster and risk reduction: earner identifies safe places and activities in the school.

Link to other learning area:

Safety issues can be reinforced when learners carry out stretches in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:
